name: Ability Gate
description: The door that asks what you have become: a passage or terrain feature that checks acquired powers and stays shut until the player owns the answer. It owns the requirement list and the pass/reject decision, and it owns them alone — it deliberately does not grant anything, because progression.power_up_grant is the only component allowed to mutate what the player can do, and a gate that also hands out powers hides progression inside geography. Its sibling world.door_gate checks the level's current state (switches, plates); this gate checks the player's accumulated state, and the distinction matters because the two open on different evidence and fail for different reasons. The rejection path is a first-class output: a gate that silently refuses teaches nothing, so the missing-power list is published for whatever hint or UI layer wants it rather than rendered here.

inputs.name: requiredPowerIds
inputs.description: Power ids the player must hold — matching progression.power_up_grant's powerId values — for this gate to pass.

inputs.name: requireAll
inputs.description: True demands every listed power (compound gates for late-game shortcuts); false passes on any one (multiple valid solutions to one obstacle).

inputs.name: permanentlyOpen
inputs.description: Once passed, stay open. Almost always true in a metroidvania — re-checking on every revisit turns backtracking, the genre's core pleasure, into a chore.

inputs.name: blocksEnemiesToo
inputs.description: Whether the gate physically obstructs everything or filters by the player's powers only. Filtering is the default; a gate that also walls off enemies changes encounter design, not just access.

outputs.name: missingPowerIds
outputs.description: The powers the player still lacks, published so a hint system can answer 'not yet — you need the wall-cling' without reimplementing the check.
